claims.text: A geometric approach using convex hull analysis on spatial response embeddings quantifies uncertainty in large language models.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on prompt complexity.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on the specific model evaluated.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on the temperature setting.

evidence.description: The proposed method leverages the spatial properties of response embeddings to measure the dispersion and variability of model outputs via convex hull analysis.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the prompt complexity.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the model.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the temperature setting.

methodologies.name: Convex Hull Analysis on Response Embeddings
methodologies.description: Converts LLM outputs into BERT embeddings, projects them to 2D via PCA, clusters them with DBSCAN, and computes the convex hull of clusters to measure dispersion.

limitations.text: Traditional methods for uncertainty quantification, such as probabilistic models and ensemble techniques, face challenges when applied to the complex and high-dimensional nature of LLM-generated outputs.
